role: User-requested class balancing of the three-genre feasibility study; development comparison, not a pristine final evaluation
target: Author preference among Mystery, Thriller, Romance; weights belong to preference groups, not to the input book genre
data_and_folds: Exactly the existing three-group cohorts and three book-disjoint outer folds, same inner book-disjoint holdout; one review per author
training_weights: Within each training subset only, w_g = N_train / (3 * N_train_g); average weight 1 and equal total weight per group
test_weights: No sample weighting, resampling or distribution changes in the held-out folds. Report macro-F1, balanced accuracy, ordinary accuracy, per-group precision/recall/F1 and prediction frequency
main_models: Same seven logistic feature sets, same three regularization options selected on inner macro-F1; weighted mean cross-entropy plus unchanged L2 penalty
naive_bayes: Report both a balanced weighted-count fit with Laplace smoothing 1 and uniform class priors, and a prior-only variant with original class-conditional counts and uniform priors. Distinguish these two changes explicitly.
unweighted_comparator: Reuse the frozen unweighted out-of-fold predictions and assert exact author/book/truth/fold alignment. Do not overwrite previous results.
uncertainty: 2000 paired book bootstrap resamples for changes in metrics and each group's precision/recall, holding predictions fixed
schemes: Thriller-input subset of the exact same selected reviews
no_more_options: No new vocabulary, representations, sampling methods, thresholds or regularization grid values in response to outcomes
scope: Keep the current three-group objective. Reassess training policy and qualify earlier unweighted conclusions.
